sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns or true/false).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) The hour hand of a clock turns through ____ in 30 minutes. (ii) The area swept by a 10 cm minute hand in 20 minutes is ____.
questions.answer:
(i) The hour hand turns 30° per hour, so 15° in 30 minutes.
(ii) 20 minutes = 120° = ⅓ of a turn: ⅓ × 22/7 × 10² = 2200/21 ≈ 104.76 cm².

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) The area of a parallelogram of area 18 cm² on a base of 6 cm has height ____. (ii) The area of an isosceles triangle with base 12 cm and equal sides 10 cm is ____.
questions.answer:
(i) Height = area ÷ base = 18 ÷ 6 = 3 cm.
(ii) Height = √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm; area = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 cm².

questions.q: Write True or False: (i) The area of a sector of radius 6 cm with arc 11 cm is 33 cm². (ii) The circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm is 22 cm.
questions.answer:
(i) True: area = ½ × l × r = ½ × 11 × 6 = 33 cm².
(ii) False: 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44 cm.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) A rectangle with sides in the ratio 5 : 2 and perimeter 98 cm has area ____. (ii) The area of a triangle with base 7 cm and height 6 cm is ____.
questions.answer:
(i) 2(5k + 2k) = 98 ⇒ k = 7; sides 35 and 14; area = 490 cm².
(ii) ½ × 7 × 6 = 21 cm².

A circular path 2 m wide runs inside the boundary of a circular park of radius 16 m. Find the cost of paving it at ₹24 per m². (π = 3.14)
A circular field is bought at ₹7,000 per m² for ₹31,68,000. Find the cost of fencing it at ₹140 per metre.
Two perpendicular paths, each 10 m wide, run through the middle of a 200 m × 150 m park. Find the cost of constructing them at ₹50 per m².
questions.answer:
Path along the length: 200 × 10 = 2000 m². Path along the breadth: 150 × 10 = 1500 m².
Common square 10 × 10 = 100 m² is counted twice.
Area = 2000 + 1500 − 100 = 3400 m². Cost = 3400 × 50 = ₹1,70,000.

questions.q: A rectangular park 30 m × 20 m has two paths each 2 m wide around it, one inside and one outside. Find the cost of paving them at ₹50 per m².
A square of side 4 cm is inscribed in a circle. Find the area enclosed between the circle and the square. (π = 22/7)
questions.answer:
The diagonal of the square is a diameter: d = 4√2 cm, so r = 2√2 cm and r² = 8.
Area of circle = 22/7 × 8 = 176/7 ≈ 25.14 cm².
Area of square = 16 cm².
Required area = 25.14 − 16 = 9.14 cm².

questions.q: A horse is tied with a 14 m rope at one corner of a rectangular field 40 m × 30 m. Find (i) the area it can graze (ii) the area it cannot graze (iii) the increase in grazing area if the rope were 21 m.
questions.answer:
The corner angle is 90°, so the horse grazes a quarter circle.
(i) ¼ × 22/7 × 14² = ¼ × 616 = 154 m².
(ii) Field = 40 × 30 = 1200 m²; not grazed = 1200 − 154 = 1046 m².
(iii) With 21 m: ¼ × 22/7 × 441 = 346.5 m²; increase = 346.5 − 154 = 192.5 m².

questions.q: Find the area of a trapezium whose parallel sides are 25 cm and 10 cm and whose non-parallel sides are 14 cm and 13 cm.
questions.answer:
Draw a line from one end of the shorter side parallel to the non-parallel side of 14 cm. It cuts off a triangle with sides 14, 13 and 25 − 10 = 15 cm.
s = (14 + 13 + 15)/2 = 21; area of triangle = √[21 × 7 × 8 × 6] = √7056 = 84 cm².
Height of the triangle (= height of the trapezium) on base 15: ½ × 15 × h = 84 ⇒ h = 11.2 cm.
Area of trapezium = ½ × (25 + 10) × 11.2 = 196 cm².
